headline: ICT judges inspect 'Aynaghar' detention cell at Rab-1
summary: Judges of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) visited the secret prisons of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), looking into allegations of enforced disappearances.
details: Judges of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) conducted an inspection of the Rapid Action Battalion's (RAB) TFI cell, commonly known as 'Aynaghar' (the House of Mirrors), at the Rab-1 headquarters in Dhaka.

The inspection was part of an ongoing investigation into the secret detention centers used by the RAB to hold prisoners without legal process, which has been a long-standing allegation of human rights own violations.
The Chief Prosecutor's office stated that those involved in the operation of these secret prisons will be brought to justice under the law.
Additionally, the Chief Prosecutor warned that strict action will be taken against anyone involved in the destruction of evidence related to 'Aynaghar'.
The visit by the ICT judges was accompanied by various officials and prosecution teams, as the judges examined the cells and the facilities provided to the detainees.
The inspection highlights the continuing legal scrutiny of the RAB's and the previous administration's use of secret detention facilities to silence dissent.
caption:
Inside the 'House of Mirrors': ICT judges inspect RAB's secret detention cells.

Judges of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) conducted an inspection of the Rapid Action Battalion's (RAB) TFI cell, commonly known as 'Aynaghar' (the House of Mirrors), at the Rab-1 headquarters in Dhaka.

The inspection was part of an ongoing investigation into the secret detention centers used by the RAB to hold prisoners without legal process, which has been a long-standing allegation of human rights own violations.

The Chief Prosecutor's office stated that those involved in the operation of these secret prisons will be brought to justice under the law.

Additionally, the Chief Prosecutor warned that strict action will be taken against anyone involved in the destruction of evidence related to 'Aynaghar'.

The visit by the ICT judges was accompanied by various officials and prosecution teams, as the judges examined the cells and the facilities provided to the detainees.

The inspection highlights the continuing legal scrutiny of the RAB's and the previous administration's use of secret detention facilities to silence dissent.

headline: 14,384 primary teachers to join from October 29
summary: The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education announced the joining date for recommended assistant teachers after delays due to investigation and procedural issues.
details: The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education has announced that 14,384 recommended assistant teachers will join their duties on October 29.
The decision was made following an emergency virtual meeting held at the ministry on Saturday, August 1.
Primary and Mass Education Secretary Md. Sakhawat Hossain stated that the government is prioritizing the appointment of these teachers.
He explained that the process was delayed due to investigations and procedural formalities.
Once the teachers join on October 29, they will undergo professional training following their appointment.
caption:
14,384 new primary teachers are finally joining the workforce on October 29.

He explained that the process was delayed due to investigations and procedural formalities.

Once the teachers join on October 29, they will undergo professional training following their appointment.
